text:
dan: quick brain dump - i've been chasing unpredictable tail-latency on hosts with mixed numa vms. hypothesis: interleaved frees across numa nodes prevent useful coalescing and cause repeated remote allocations. thinking we need a 'shadow free ring' per-tenant+numa that delays reclaim into a coalescing-friendly window.

yara: can you sketch how shadow ring differs from our opportunistic coalesce today? :thinking_face:

dan: current free path immediately merges into per-arena free lists -> fragmentation. shadow ring would buffer frees for ~50-200ms (config) and then drain them into a coalescer that is numa-local and page-colored aware. small frees (<64B) still go fast-path but mark for shadowing if they are cross-node.

mo: so frees are deferred. are we worried about reserved memory pressure / perceived leak? how do we account for billing/evict decisions?

dan: good call. plan: shadow entries are accounted in a "soft_free" gauge (visible to admission and billing as not-yet-returned). eviction/admission must treat soft_free as reclaimable but slower. Billing should only consider fully freed bytes as reclaimable; we emit events on drain commit to adjust any billing deltas.

yara: interesting. page-coloring + numa-local coalescer sounds heavy. how do we ensure the coalescer finds contiguous runs across fragmented freelists?

dan: coalescer will work on a compacted bitmap per-arena (256B granularity) and run a stitching pass that prefers colors matching local numa node. We'll keep a tiny per-arena "stitch reserve" to avoid global stalls. Also use heuristics: only attempt full coalesce if contiguous_estimate < X or on low-qps windows.

mo: API proposal?

dan: rough API:

```
Allocator.DeferFree(addr, size, tenant, numa) -> shadow_id
Allocator.DrainShadow(arena, budget_ms) -> bytes_reclaimed
Allocator.ForceDrain(tenant) -> job_id
Allocator.ContigEstimate(arena) -> bytes
```
Drains commit frees in batches and emit commit events with (tenant, bytes, duration).

yara: test matrix: synthetic cross-node free pattern, mixed small/large alloc, and real trace replay with tenant-noise. we also need to simulate crash/restart - shadow ring must persist or be replay-safe.

dan: yep — shadow metadata needs to be durable enough to not lose accounting. Persisting every free is expensive; we'll checkpoint shadow rings periodically and on graceful shutdown. On crash, we conservatively assume shadows are not freed and update gauges accordingly.

mo: perf risk: added latency on free path (defer write) and memory pressure due to delayed reclamation. What's the recommended default delay?

dan: start with 100ms conservative default, feature-flag for 50ms in sandbox. Also add an adaptive mode: if fragmentation ratio > 0.25, increase delay to allow coalescer to aggregate more; if contig_est grows, shrink delay.

yara: telemetry: add gauges shadow_bytes_by_tenant, shadow_depth_histogram, shadow_drain_duration_ms, contig_estimate_bytes, fragmentation_ratio. Add alert if shadow_bytes_by_tenant / resident > 0.2 for 2m -> P3.

allocator-bot: perf job created: shadow-ring-eval-20240601 (id: job-20240601-21)

mo: correctness: need to ensure no use-after-free — i.e., any ptr handed back earlier must be safe. Defer only when allocation is fully logically freed and no refcounts; don't defer if caller expects immediate mmaps/munmap semantics. Add API flag: Free(immediate=true|false).

dan: good point. we'll only defer frees that come from internal vm-abstractions where we control refs. Expose a config knob to force immediate free for debug.

yara: one more: consider combining with slab-tagging: tag allocations with color + tenant; on free, place into color-buckets so drain can stitch same-color runs cheaply. simplifies bitmap scanning.
dan: love it. add slab tags. implementation steps:
1) prototype shadow ring collector + durable checkpointing (dan)
2) add color-tagging on alloc/free and coalescer that prefers same-color stitching (yara)
3) telemetry + alerts (mo)
4) perf runs + crash recovery tests (everyone)

mo: add a clash-case: small-kv churn where shadowing increases working set too much. we need an escape hatch: policy to short-circuit shadowing for tenants with hot-write_ratio > threshold.

allocator-bot: reminder: open RFC template: /docs/rfcs/shadow-free-ring.md

dan: i'll draft RFC and attach perf traces. thanks all :thumbsup:
